tpms.when: 2007 (low tire pressure warning light, no driver reset button)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the tire information placard on the driver's door jamb.
Turn the ignition on and drive normally. Once the pressures are right, the low tire pressure light should stay out; there is no button to press.
If the light stays on or returns soon after, check each tire again for a leak or flat and fit the spare if needed.
tpms.note: If the light flashes for about a minute and then stays on, the monitoring system has a fault that adding air will not fix; have a dealer check it.

tpms.when: 2011 (low tire pressure warning light, no driver reset button)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the tire information placard on the driver's door jamb, before driving or after the vehicle has sat a few hours.
If you are filling them in a garage warmer than outside, add about 1 psi for every 10°F of difference.
Turn the ignition on and drive normally. With the pressures corrected, the low tire pressure light should go out by itself; there is no reset button.
If the light comes back soon after filling, a tire is probably leaking or flat: stop somewhere safe and check it.
At high altitude the light may stay on at the placard pressure; adding a little air above the placard figure clears it.
tpms.note: If the light flashes for about a minute and then stays on, the system has a fault that adding air will not fix; have a dealer check it. Check the light after fitting different tires or wheels.
